featured_reviews.name: Dennis K
featured_reviews.review_text:
I moved to Bombay from a small town 5 years ago and got connected to Avatar. My first impression of this community was; "If Bombay had a face, these guys should be it." I couldn't help but notice how such a bunch of talented young professionals, entrepreneurs, entertainment industry professionals, musicians, social workers, parents, and drifters somehow all managed to gather under one roof. Honestly, I would never expect busy Bombay folk to have the time to show up on a Sunday morning for something as tedious as church. And still, i could see how people were being drawn to this place every Sunday.
This community has challenged so many of my self-seeking world views and has continuously provided some great perspective on God's heart for me. I have forged many great friendships here that i will carry with me for the rest of my life.
I am really thankful for the effort made here to reveal the good news of Christ in a relevant way without watering down anything, but rather pushing for the truth to move forward in our lives.
One of the memories i really love about Avatar is from the time we used to hold our Sunday meetings in someone's living room and how the place smelled of freshly brewed coffee as you entered in. And then you got to drink it..
I highly recommend this place. I have personally found this is to be a great place to meet God, experience God's love and learn how to impact your world.

featured_reviews.name: Melissa Henderson
featured_reviews.review_text: I was a part of the Avatar community for 6 years. My biggest concern when moving to Mumbai from the US was about whether I would find a good church in such a huge city. I had heard about Avatar even before I got to India, and during my first week in Mumbai, one of my colleagues brought me to Avatar. As soon as the service started I felt home <3. I have not even tried any other churches till date! Avatar is a good mix of locals and expats, and they really love people well. I felt so welcome there, and they invite all with open arms! This community really became my family in Mumbai. I couldn't have stayed in Mumbai for 6 years if it wasn't for NLF, and I will never forget my time with this COMMUNITY. That is really what Avatar is. Yes, the services are great - the worship and word - and I definitely grew closer to God while I attended Avatar. But events, programs, and the building aside, they really embody Philippians 1:3-11 for me. Love you guys!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Mount Mary Church on Christmas Eve, and as expected, the place was absolutely flooded with people. The festive vibe was beautiful and full of energy, but be prepared for heavy crowds if you’re visiting on special occasions.

Since the hill road leading up to the church was barricaded for public transport, we had to walk around 500–600 meters uphill to reach the church. The walk was manageable and actually added to the whole experience, especially with the festive atmosphere all around.

The church itself is very well maintained. Despite the massive crowd, everything felt organized. The traffic flow, entry and exit movement, and crowd management were handled quite efficiently. Even the toilets were surprisingly clean, which is commendable considering the rush.

Outside the church, there were several local shops selling candles, small toys for kids, and other religious items. You’ll also find a few local food joints around the area, making it convenient to grab a quick bite.

Overall, it was a spiritually uplifting and well-managed experience despite the heavy rush. A solid four-star visit for the festive charm, cleanliness, and efficient crowd handling. Would definitely recommend visiting—just plan ahead during peak occasions! ✨

featured_reviews.name: Roosa and Gigi
featured_reviews.review_text:

The church itself is simple but really beautiful. Inside, it’s quiet and gives you that space to just sit, think, or pray without feeling rushed. A lot of people come here for devotion, but even if you’re just visiting, there’s a very calming atmosphere that’s hard to ignore.
Outside, the sea breeze and the surroundings make it even more relaxing. It’s also quite popular, especially during the feast, when the whole area gets lively with stalls and people. That side feels more festive, but on regular days it’s much more laid-back.
It is a nice place to visit whether you’re religious or not. It’s peaceful, scenic, and has a kind of quiet charm that makes you want to slow down a bit.

featured_reviews.name: Ghumakkad Delhiite
featured_reviews.review_text:
Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount

Popularly known as Mount Mary Church, this historic Roman Catholic basilica stands on a hill in Bandra, Mumbai, overlooking the Arabian Sea. Originally established by Portuguese settlers in the 17th century, the present structure was built in 1904 in a beautiful Gothic style. The church is dedicated to the Virgin Mary and houses a revered statue believed by many to be miraculous. It attracts devotees of all faiths, especially during the annual Bandra Fair in September. Scenes from the famous Bollywood film Amar Akbar Anthony were shot here. We visited the church in December 2025 and experienced its peaceful atmosphere and scenic sea views.

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Mumbai during Christmas, Mount Mary Basilica in Bandra is pure magic. Walking up that hill in December feels like stepping into a festive postcard. The church is draped in warm lights, nativity scenes, and candles that make the whole place glow beautifully against the night sky. It’s not flashy—just elegant and serene.

The vibe? Honestly, it’s a mix of devotion and celebration. Families, friends, even solo visitors gather around, some praying quietly, others just soaking in the atmosphere. I loved how inclusive it felt—people from all walks of life sharing smiles and festive treats. If you go, try to reach by evening; the lights look stunning after sunset.

The carol nights were a highlight for me. Choirs from across Mumbai filled the air with music that gave me goosebumps. And Midnight Mass? Absolutely moving. Candlelight, hymns, and that sense of peace you rarely find in a bustling city—it’s unforgettable.

After the church visit, don’t miss the Bandra Wonderland along Carter Road and Reclamation. It’s like the festive spirit spilled onto the streets—light tunnels, Christmas trees, food stalls, and music. Perfect way to end the night.

Why you should go:
Gorgeous décor and peaceful ambience
Soulful carols and a heartfelt Midnight Mass
A mix of spirituality and community warmth
Bonus: seaside lights and festive stalls nearby

If you’re looking for a Christmas experience that’s both spiritual and joyful, Mount Mary during the holidays is a must. It’s not just a visit—it’s a feeling you carry home.

The architecture combines grandeur with serenity and offers a visually rich and spiritually enriching experience for visitors.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, colloquially known as Mount Bandra and Mount St Mary Church; is a basilica (shrine) of the Roman Catholic Church, located at the Bandra neighbourhood of Bombay (Mumbai), India.

The story of Mount Mary Church in Bandra begins in the 1570s when Jesuit priests built a small mud-and-stone oratory on a hill overlooking the Arabian Sea in Bandra. They brought a statue of Our Lady to this location, and this event marked the beginning of the shrine's history.

The original statue is believed to have been miraculously recovered after being thrown into the sea, and a more permanent basilica was later built on the site, which has become a place of pilgrimage and peace for people of all faiths, particularly Hindus and Christians. The current church, a semi-Gothic structure, was rebuilt in 1904 and is now known as the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount.

The Old Church: The foundation of the original St Peter’s Church was laid in April 12, 1852, by Bishop Hartmann. The Church was completed in September 1853. It measured approximately 100 by 75 feet. In 1867 a second storey was added to the old top floor.
The storey above the Church was at first used as the priests’ residence and parish school. In 1855, the Jesuit Seminary was transferred from Surat to Bandra, and the seminary and the parish schools were merged. In 1863, the seminary was again transferred to Bombay, and the Boys’ Orphanage from Bombay came to Bandra. This was the beginning of the St Stanislaus’ High School.

The New Church: As far back as August 1887, the then Archbishop of Bombay issued the following appeal: “The poor parish of St. Peter’s Bandora, numbers with the orphans (boys and girls) 2215 souls and has for a church the floor of the boys’ Orphanage. This place is much too small and is ill-suited for divine service. A new and more spacious Church is much needed and will be a great benefit to the poor Parishioners and the Orphans”.

The growing needs of the parish necessitated the building of a larger Church, and so in September, 1938, Archbishop Thomas Roberts, S.J. blessed the foundation stone of the present St Peter’s Church.

The new Church has been built on the site of the old and has been designed on the Romanesque style, this is one of the best example of awesome architecture! Every where you see in this church will leave you awestruck! You'll be confused to decide what and where to see! The alter is pretty basic but holds a significant meaning! The statue of Risen Christ immediately makes you feel like home!
It is easily accessible from Bandra station! One can walk for 15 min to reach here or taken an sharing auto or the best BEST BUS (211, 214, 219 all AC charging just 6/-).
If you're visiting mount mary add this church in your must visit church list!

St Vincent De Paul Church is more than a place of worship—it is a layered story of faith, time, and community, expressed through five defining pillars:

Miracles
Stories of quiet grace echo through generations—answered prayers, moments of healing, and an unspoken belief that faith here finds its way. The church carries an aura where the intangible feels deeply personal.

Heritage
Rooted in the legacy of Chuim village, its origins date back to the 1940s, evolving alongside Mumbai’s transformation while preserving its old-world soul and spiritual continuity.

Architecture
A harmonious blend of simplicity and purpose, its structure balances modern functionality with sacred calm—featuring serene interiors, soft natural light, and spaces designed for reflection.

Parishioners
The heartbeat of the church—diverse yet deeply connected. Generations of families shape its identity, carrying forward traditions with warmth, service, and collective faith.

Activities
Beyond prayer, it thrives as a hub of engagement—community outreach, youth initiatives, charitable work, and celebrations that bind people together in purpose and spirit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bandra Fair is a week-long celebration held every September at the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount in Bandra, Mumbai. It celebrates the birthday of Mother Mary (September 8th). This festival is over 300 years old and is loved by people of all religions.
Important Dates for 2026
The fair traditionally begins on the first Sunday after September 8th.
• Start Date: Sunday, September 13, 2026
• End Date: Sunday, September 20, 2026
Why is it special?
• Spiritual Tradition: Devotees visit the beautiful hilltop church to pray and light candles. Many offer wax figures (like a house or a heart) to ask for specific blessings.
• The Food: The lanes are filled with stalls selling traditional snacks. You must try Mumbra (sweet pancakes), Kadio Bodio (tiny ginger-sugar sticks), and pink-colored "guava cheese" sweets.
• Fun & Shopping: The area turns into a giant carnival with giant wheels, games, and stalls selling toys, handmade items, and clothes.
Quick Tips for Visitors
• Location: Mount Mary Hill, Bandra West.
• Travel: Use public transport (Bus or Rickshaw) from Bandra Station, as the roads are very crowded and closed to private cars.
• Best Time: Go on a weekday morning to avoid the massive weekend crowds.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mount Mary Festival, popularly known as the Bandra Fair, is held at the Mount Mary Church, also called the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, located in Bandra, Mumbai.
Every year, Mumbai celebrates the Mount Mary Festival, popularly known as the Bandra Fair, to pay homage to Mother Mary (mother of Jesus Christ) who was born on September 8. The festival is held at the Mount Mary Church, also called the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, located in Bandra. People of various faiths attend the fair, which has become an essential part of Mumbai’s cultural fabric over the years. This festival is a lively and colourful event that attracts a large number of visitors. The Mount Mary Festival is a grand annual event that spans about a week.
Every year, the festival begins on the first Sunday after September 8. Mount Mary Fair will be held this year from September 10 to September 17. The fair is open to the public from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. Those who wish to attend should consult the notice board in the church or keep an eye out for activities taking place throughout the day.
According to folktales, the fair began when a statue of St. Mary was discovered floating in the Arabian Sea, which borders the cathedral. It had been a dream of a Koli fisherman a few years before. Many devotees seek blessings from this holy statue. The festival takes place in the Mount Mary Church complex and the alleys around the church. The celebrations are similar to a funfair which includes games, concerts, and amusement rides. During the event, there are kiosks selling Goan and Maharashtrian cuisine. They also sell sweets, handcrafted cakes and fudges, chikki, and other delectable treats.

The Mount Mary Church is in Bandra, Mumbai. Its history dates back to the 16th century, when the Portuguese initially built a small church on this hill. Over the years, the church has undergone several changes and renovations, evolving into the magnificent structure that stands today. This site holds immense importance for Christians and is considered one of the holiest places. The Koli community in Bandra affectionately call this statue ‘Moti Mauli’ in Marathi, which means ‘Pearl Mother.’

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a beautiful Roman Catholic Church which is very famous for the week-long Bandra fair which takes place here every year in September.

This Basilica, build by the portuguese in 1705, has stood the test of time, and the current building, already a hundred years now, is a photographer's paradise, and a serene experience of faith and prayers inside.

Be sure to capture the rustic paintings on the ceiling and the 12 apostles on the walls. It will give you an old world charm, and yet when you step out, this is one of the most elite (expensive) places to live in, in Mumbai. Several film personalities live around this Basilica.
It does get crowded on festivals and weekends, a great time to visit is any weekday afternoon.

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Andrew’s Church, with its 400+ years of rich history, has recently undergone a transformative 20-month renovation that beautifully preserves its heritage while rejuvenating its spiritual ambiance.

✨ Architectural Revival
Façade and Roof Rejuvenation: Heritage specialists like Jivraj Sankhat and Savani Heritage Conservation expertly restored the church’s iconic roof, façade, marble, woodwork, and stained-glass windows, reviving their original splendor.

Traditional Techniques: The renovation prioritized authenticity. Over 5.5 ft thick walls were replastered with lime instead of cement—an effort to maintain the church’s historical integrity.

🌞 Rediscovered Beauty
Choir Loft & Lighting: Long-hidden architectural gems, such as the choir loft’s clerestory windows, were uncovered—reintroducing natural light into the nave and restoring a key visual element of the original design.

💒 Interior Elegance
Faithfully Restored Altars: The Portuguese-inspired altars, once scarred by moisture and termite damage, were carefully conserved and revived to their former glory.

Wooden Pulpit Revival: Carved with biblical narrative, the original pulpit was meticulously restored, complete with its ornate canopy—allowing worshippers to once more feel its spiritual resonance.

⏳ Heritage Sensitivity & Community Effort
Meticulous, Not Hasty: From April 2024 to December 2025, the renovation focused on preservation over superficial repairs—respecting the church’s Portuguese colonial architecture.

Community-Driven, Funded by Love: Entirely financed by parishioners and diaspora support, the project faced financial hurdles—yet the community’s unwavering commitment ensured the work reached its homestretch.

🎖 A Joyous Reopening
On a beautiful Sunday evening, over a thousand worshippers celebrated the church’s rededication—blessed by Cardinal Oswald Gracias—marking a poignant return to its rightful spiritual grandeur.

In summary, the recent renovations at St. Andrew’s Church masterfully balance respect for its centuries-old heritage with modern integrity. From the reimagined façade to the restored interior treasures, every detail reflects love, care, and unwavering faith. It’s a testament to what can be achieved when a community unites to preserve its legacy—and a spiritually uplifting sanctuary reborn.
